pseudos.text: In a sincere effort to adapt and survive for the long term, the tax-software company is undergoing organizational change. The company's leader communicated the difficult decision directly to staff, resulting in a workforce reduction affecting roughly 17% of its employees. To support those leaving, the company is providing a structured support package, offering 16 weeks of base pay plus two weeks per year of tenure. This painful but necessary reinvention aims to build a stronger, more focused future together.

The tax-software company is consolidating operations, with offices in Reno and Woodland Hills winding down. This office closure is part of a business strategy to co-locate teams in strategic hubs. While a significant portion of the workforce will be affected, colleagues deserving protection and fair support have been offered severance and transition support provided. The chief executive hopes this change, though painful, will help the company renew itself for the future.

Following a corporate announcement from the company leader, about 3,000 full-time roles are planned for elimination. This job elimination is part of a stated reason for the change: to accelerate AI-driven product work. Affected workers have been offered a severance package, a gesture of care and support for those leaving. The hope is that this organizational downsizing, while disruptive, will allow the company to focus its energy in key locations.
